mappings.note: Whom the poet calls blessed (the child's mother) -- plain content recall. Rejected LO-7, which fits the 'why is she blessed' form of the same idea (item 106).
Which shabd-shakti the poem uses (abhidha) -- a kaavya-shaastra feature of expression, i.e. kala-paksh. Rejected LO-2 because shabd-shakti is not chhand, tuk, lay, yati or the poem's bhaasha/boli.
Asks the poem's BHAASHA (Sanskritnishth khadi boli) -- the medium/form of the poem. Rejected LO-7 because language register here is a formal property, not bhaav-paksh or kala-paksh interpretation.
Whose smile the phrase is used for (the poet's infant) -- content recall. Rejected LO-7 since only the referent is named, with no interpretation of the image.
Which kaavya-GUN the poem has (maadhurya and prasaad) -- an explicit kala-paksh category. Rejected LO-2 because gun is not a form element like chhand or lay.
Which RAS predominates (vaatsalya) -- ras is listed under kaavya-saundarya/bhaav-paksh. Rejected LO-2, which covers only tuk, lay, yati, gati and the poem's form.
What the child's body is like (dhool-dhoosarit) -- literal recall of the poem's word. Rejected LO-7 because the upamaan is not asked for here.
Asks for WHOM the poet uses 'kamal' -- the referent of the poem's rupak/upamaan (the infant). Rejected LO-5: the stem never names or asks to identify the alankaar itself.
What changed at the child's touch (shefaalika flowers fell) -- literal content. Rejected LO-7, which fits the 'what do those changes signify' framing rather than this recall.
Whose amrit-laden influence nourished the crops (the rivers') -- recall from the poem. Rejected LO-7 because the 'amrit' image is not itself being explained.
The pen-name Nagarjuna wrote under in Maithili (Yatri) -- poet biography, and this thin frame has no biography LO. Rejected LO-6 as the fact is nowhere in the poem.
Which flower blooms in the hut (kamal) -- literal content. Rejected LO-7, which fits the 'what does the lotus in the hut mean' form (items 2, 113).
How many rivers' water the poem mentions (many) -- literal detail. Rejected LO-7 as no image is decoded.
Gloss of 'dhooli-dhoosar gaat', the poem's own phrase. Rejected C-H1.2 because it is poem diction, not a decontextualised vocabulary drill.
Gloss of 'jaljaat' (kamal) as used in the poem. Rejected C-H1.2 for the same reason -- the word carries poem content.
Gloss of 'itar' (= doosra) as the poet uses it of himself. Rejected C-H1.2 because the trap option (perfume) only makes sense against the poem's line, so this tests kaavyabodh.
Subject-matter of 'Fasal' -- content comprehension. Rejected LO-2, which would apply only to its chhand or bhaasha. (Duplicate of item 14.)
Whose magic yields the crop (river water) -- naming the referent the poem states. Rejected LO-7, kept for the item that asks what 'paani ka jaadu' MEANS (items 90, 103).
Explicit 'aashay' of 'sandali mitti' -- unpacking the poem's sensory image. Rejected LO-6 because the item asks the sense of the epithet, not a fact.
Who teaches the crop to sway (the wind) -- literal recall. Rejected LO-7: although 'thirakna' is a maanaveekaran, the stem asks only the agent, not the device or its effect.
What the crop is per the poet -- the poem's stated position on labour plus nature. Rejected LO-7 as no interpretive or aesthetic demand is made.
Nagarjuna's real name (Vaidyanath Mishra) -- poet biography; no biography LO exists, so the competency is the honest parent. Rejected LO-6 because the fact is outside the poem.
The poet's year of birth -- literary-history fact. Rejected LO-6 for the same reason: nothing in the poem's text supplies it.
Why Maithili society withheld respect from Nagarjuna -- biographical/literary history. Rejected LO-6 because it is not a kaavyabodh question about the prescribed poems.
Which listed work is NOT Nagarjuna's -- bibliography. Rejected LO-6: the poem's content plays no part.
Which kaavya-dhaara Nagarjuna belongs to (pragatisheel janvaadi) -- literary history. Rejected LO-7 because the item classifies the poet, not the poem's saundarya.
Recall of whose touch the crop is called the garima of. Rejected LO-7, which is kept for the 'kya abhipraay' form of this same line (item 20). (Duplicate of item 12.)
Whose transformed form the crops are (the sun's rays) -- direct recall. Rejected LO-7 as the significance of the transformation is not asked. (Duplicate of item 23.)
Who wrote 'Fasal' -- authorship, i.e. literary history with no biography LO available. Rejected LO-6 because the answer is not in the poem's content.
Asks the MEANING of 'paani ka jaadu' (= water's effect) -- decoding the metaphor. Rejected LO-6 because the literal magic readings are the distractors.
Whose koti-koti hands are meant (the farmers') -- naming the agent, plain comprehension. Rejected LO-7, reserved for the item asking what that garima expresses (item 120).
What the poet calls 'haathon ke sparsh ki mahima' (the crop) -- the referent of a rupak predication. Rejected LO-6 because the phrase is figurative and must be interpreted, not looked up.
Which noun 'sandali' qualifies in the poem (mitti) -- textual recall. Rejected LO-7, which fits the item asking the aashay of sandali mitti (item 79).
What is called 'mitti ka gundharm' (the crop) -- a rupak referent, the pattern policy assigns to kala-paksh. Rejected LO-6 because the equation is metaphorical, not stated as fact.
What the wind helps grow (the crops) -- literal content. Rejected LO-7 as no image or craft feature is analysed.

Gloss of the poem's coinage 'danturit muskaan'. Rejected LO-7 despite the 'taatparya' wording: the answer is the meaning of the word (a newly-teethed child's smile), same as item 41, not an aesthetic reading.
Whose mother the poet blesses -- plain content. Rejected LO-7, kept for the 'why' version of this question (item 106).
Asks what the poem is like from the CHHAND point of view -- chhand is named outright in LO-2. Rejected LO-7 because metre is a form element, not kaavya-saundarya.
aashay of 'kankhi maarna' as it occurs in the poem. Rejected C-H1.2: muhaavare go to the grammar competency only when the item carries no poem content, and this one glosses the poem's own diction.
Which RAS predominates in the poem -- ras sits under kaavya-saundarya/bhaav-paksh. Rejected LO-2, which covers only the poem's formal units.
The SHAILI of 'Fasal' -- style is listed as kala-paksh. Rejected LO-2 because shaili is not chhand, tuk, lay or the language itself (that is the sibling item 102).
The BHAASHA of 'Fasal' -- the poem's medium. Rejected LO-7, which takes the neighbouring shaili question (item 101); language register is a form property.
taatparya of the metaphor 'paani ka jaadu'. Rejected LO-6 because the item asks what the figure conveys, not which element the poem names.

Explicitly asks the infant's MANAHSTHITI to be described -- bhaav-paksh. Rejected LO-6 since the 'when' half is only a lead-in to the emotional description. (Stem is OCR-damaged: 'agigesh' for animesh, 'usakar' for uski.)
Difference between a child's smile and an adult's -- a kaavyabodh question answered from the poem's sense. Rejected LO-7 because no specific image, ras or shilp feature is under analysis.
Why the poet calls the infant's mother blessed -- reason drawn from the poem's narrative. Rejected LO-7 as the answer is situational, not an aesthetic judgement.
Which gesture of the child prompts the quoted line -- content recall keyed to a specific line. Rejected LO-7 because the line is not figurative and needs no decoding.
With whose help the poet saw the smile (the mother) -- plain content. Rejected LO-7 as nothing aesthetic is probed.
Why the poet calls himself pravaasi, itar and atithi -- the reason is his long absence, a narrative fact of the poem. Rejected LO-7 because the epithets are literal, not prateek.
Which changes the child's touch brought -- an inventory of the poem's stated transformations. Rejected LO-7, which would fit asking what those transformations signify.
How the dust-covered body SEEMED to the poet -- the upamaan (kamal) and the feeling it evoked. Rejected LO-6 because the answer is the comparison, not the fact of the dust. Parallel to item 9.
Infer the child's age from 'danturit muskaan' with reasons -- inference from the poem's content. Rejected LO-7 as the reasoning is about facts, not kaavya-saundarya.
aashay of the lotus blooming in the hut (joy amid poverty) -- image interpretation. Rejected LO-6 because the literal flower reading is the distractor. (Duplicate of item 2.)
Who is gazing at the poet (the infant) -- plain content. Rejected LO-7 as nothing is interpreted.

What the smile can melt, keyed to the hard person's MIND -- the paashaan image decoded. Rejected LO-6 because the literal stone option is present and wrong. (Duplicate of item 1; stem carries a stray 'CBSE' source tag.)
Whose smile is so captivating (the infant's) -- naming the referent. Rejected LO-7, kept for the item asking what the murde-mein-jaan line means (item 117).
Asks the MEANING of the atishayokti 'murde mein jaan daal deti hai' -- hope restored to the despairing. Rejected LO-6 because the literal revival option is the distractor. (Duplicate of item 27.)
Asks what the infant's body blooms LIKE -- the upamaan (kamal) of the poem's comparison. Rejected LO-5 because the item does not name or ask to identify upama as an alankaar.
Whom the infant stares at (the poet) -- literal content. Rejected LO-7 as no figurative reading is needed.

What the poet WANTS TO EXPRESS by calling the crop the garima and mahima of hands -- explicit abhivyakti/bhaav-paksh. Rejected LO-6 because the item goes past the line to its intent. (Stem has the OCR artefact 'fasaal'.)
